title: Oliv AI product documentation
text: Oliv brings customer activity, account context and revenue processes together so agents can help teams prospect, progress deals, serve customers and identify expansion opportunities.

title: Oliv AI product documentation · What Oliv does
text: Oliv works with an existing revenue stack. Conversations and business records become connected account and opportunity context; specialist agents use that context to prepare work, surface changes and carry out configured actions. Salesforce or HubSpot can remain the system of record. The current product presentation distinguishes three things: the context foundation, agents that perform specific jobs, and apps that organize team workflows. A team can begin with a defined use case rather than replacing its entire stack.

title: Oliv AI product documentation · Choose your starting point
text: Start with the job you want to complete. A seller preparing for a meeting needs different setup and evidence from a RevOps leader allowing CRM writes or a CS manager reviewing account health.

title: Oliv AI product documentation · Read this V1 correctly
text: This is a source-grounded review draft, not a certification that every described capability is available in every workspace. Current public product pages set the naming and presentation; accessible internal agent documents add detail; dated Help Center articles provide setup and support context. Each page separates documented behavior from unresolved rules. Source publication dates, HTTP retrieval dates and product release dates are different. A source-backed description does not establish a plan entitlement, enforced permission or guaranteed completion time.

title: Getting started
text: A successful first deployment has a clear owner, a defined input, an observable output and an agreed point where a human reviews the work.

title: Getting started · Start with one outcome
text: Choose a bounded workflow: prepare opportunity-linked meetings, propose CRM field updates, review pipeline risk or prepare account-health briefs. Establish which records and people are in scope and what success looks like before increasing volume.

title: Getting started · Recommended setup sequence
text: Confirm the app and agent entitlement for the selected users. Connect the calendar, CRM and conversation sources needed by that workflow. Provide the relevant qualification criteria, ownership rules and process exceptions. Agree review, approval and notification behavior with the implementation owner. Run a small set of representative cases, including an exception or failure, and check the resulting records.

title: Getting started · Check the deployment boundary
text: Setup instructions vary by connector and organization policy. Some public setup copy describes an assisted rollout rather than a fully self-service configuration. Obtain the current connector steps for your environment instead of assuming every named integration uses the same installation path.

title: Plan your first deployment
text: Use the first deployment to establish a dependable operating workflow, not just a visually complete demonstration.

title: Plan your first deployment · Define the implementation scope
text: Write down the job, the users, the records in scope, the expected outputs and the integrations that those outputs depend on. For a CRM update workflow, include the object and field categories; for a meeting workflow, include meeting ownership and recording method. The website offers customer-operated and Oliv-operated implementation paths. Confirm who maintains the process playbook, connector configuration, exception rules and ongoing improvements in the agreed engagement. Business owner Who accepts the output and owns the workflow Technical owner Who connects systems and resolves permission issues Scope Users, teams, accounts, opportunities and excluded records Action boundary Read, draft, write, send and human review points Evidence What proves a successful run and where it is recorded

title: Plan your first deployment · Prepare the inputs
text: Provide access to the CRM and the relevant calendars, recordings, email or collaboration sources. Identify the current revenue process and qualification framework. A process document should state actual decisions and exceptions, rather than a desired future process. Where the source is incomplete or contradictory, record the disagreement for the responsible owner. Do not fill the gap with an inferred discount rule, ownership policy or customer communication permission.

title: Plan your first deployment · Recommended acceptance checks
text: Use a representative record and verify the correct account, contact and opportunity associations. Check the proposed output against the source conversation and agreed process. Test a case that should require review and verify the actual approval destination. Confirm that a changed setting persists and that the correct user can change it. Disconnect or expire a test integration in a controlled environment and observe the user-visible failure. Record the entitlement, configuration and verified date with the accepted result.

title: Plan your first deployment · Timelines and dependencies
text: Public pages describe several setup timelines for different use cases. These are not a single service-level commitment. Connector approval, historical data access, custom process work and customer review can change the schedule. Use an agreed implementation plan with explicit milestones. This V1 does not promise a universal five-minute setup, same-week deployment or fixed time to value.

title: Connect your revenue stack · Before connecting

A logo or listed vendor is not evidence that a connector is installed or authorized for that workspace. Record how to revoke the connection and what happens to already imported data. If removal requires Oliv support, make that dependency explicit in the runbook.

title: Run a first workflow
text: Begin with a low-volume, identifiable case so the team can explain exactly what happened and why.

title: Run a first workflow · Choose a representative case
text: Select a meeting linked to an active opportunity, a CRM field update with clear evidence, or an account review with known risk signals. Avoid starting with a broad historical cleanup or a large outbound audience. Identify the expected source data and the person responsible for checking the result. Remove ambiguity about who owns an opportunity or which account a conversation concerns before judging the agent output.

title: Run a first workflow · Recommended first-run sequence
text: Confirm that the selected agent or workflow is enabled for the workspace. Check the source connections and the relevant account or opportunity. Review the applicable process rules and configured action permissions. Trigger the workflow using the verified production mechanism. Inspect the output, source evidence, destination and any approval request. Accept or reject the result through the verified interface and check the resulting state.

title: Run a first workflow · Do not use the prototype as an execution guide
text: The supplied October 15 extraction describes a frontend prototype. It records controls whose actions or persistence were not implemented in that source. Labels such as Run Agent, Clone Agent or Send therefore cannot establish the production procedure. The current V1 describes the intended workflow and verification requirements. Exact production clicks, error messages and expected save states must be confirmed in a running environment before this page becomes an end-user tutorial.

title: Platform concepts
text: Oliv’s platform story is a sequence from customer activity to connected context and useful action, with process knowledge guiding how agents operate.

title: Platform concepts · A conceptual model
text: Capture brings in the activity. Context Graph associates it with business entities. Signal Graph interprets revenue questions. Process Graph supplies the organization’s rules and exceptions. Agents prepare or execute work using that context; apps organize the related team workflows. This is a user-level explanation of the current product presentation. It is not a backend deployment diagram, a database schema or a guarantee about internal event ordering.

title: Platform concepts · Keep the concepts distinct
text: An activity is an input; a signal is an interpretation of that input; a process rule defines how the organization should act; an agent performs a job; an app is a workspace for related work. Keeping those terms separate makes it easier to explain an incorrect result and identify its owner.

title: Context Capture
text: Context Capture brings customer activity into Oliv so teams and agents can work from more than manually entered CRM notes.

title: Context Capture · Activity sources
text: The current website describes meetings, phone calls, email, messages and in-person conversations, alongside connected business records and supporting data. Availability depends on the source, integration, plan and organization configuration. For each source, distinguish metadata from full content. An event title or call log is not a transcript; a linked email is not necessarily a mailbox-wide archive. Confirm the actual imported fields, access scope and historical coverage. Online meetings Organizer, recording mode, consent, transcript and participant access Phone calls Supported dialer or capture route and recording availability Email Mailbox scope, included threads, attachments and retention Messaging Connected workspace/channel scope and supported history In-person activity Supported capture application/device and upload process CRM and usage/support data Objects, fields, event coverage and sync direction

title: Context Capture · Recording has conditions
text: The May 2026 recording guide distinguishes internally organized meetings from externally organized meetings when native recording is enabled. An external organizer can require a visible note taker and lobby admission. A claim that Oliv supports botless recording should therefore include the platform and organization prerequisites. Do not describe every meeting as botless or assume the same behavior for every conferencing tool.

title: Context Capture · Recommended verification
text: Before relying on a downstream agent, check a known activity for its content, participants, timestamps and destination record. Check what happens to private, cancelled, declined or inaccessible meetings, and how a user stops capture. Missing context can cause an incomplete result without indicating a reasoning failure. Troubleshooting should first establish whether the source activity arrived and was accessible.

title: Context Graph
text: Context Graph is the relationship layer that places customer activity against the business entities it concerns.

title: Context Graph · What the graph connects
text: The public product description associates conversations and activities with accounts, contacts and opportunities, using relationship history and conversation context rather than only an email-domain match. A useful activity association should preserve a path back to its source. Review the account, the particular opportunity and the participants before allowing an agent’s interpretation to affect a customer record.

title: Context Graph · Cases that need careful review
text: Several open opportunities at one company The activity belongs to the right product, motion and buying group A partner call mentions several customer accounts Each discussed customer is associated appropriately An acquisition changes the email domain The relationship to the prior entity remains understandable Duplicate or stale CRM accounts The active record is identified without unsafe merging Several deals discussed in one meeting Shared activity does not overwrite unrelated opportunity state

title: Context Graph · Association and CRM cleanup are separate decisions
text: Choosing the likely opportunity for an activity is not the same as authorizing a destructive CRM merge. The CRM Manager document explicitly leaves duplicate-resolution thresholds unresolved. Verify the current review and correction path for an incorrect association. This V1 does not claim a confidence threshold, automatic merge policy or guaranteed perfect mapping.

title: Context Graph · Recommended acceptance criteria
text: Use examples of multiple opportunities, duplicates and changed domains in the first deployment review. Require an explanation of the selected record, source evidence and a way to correct an incorrect association. Document whether a correction changes only the current activity or also related historical associations. That behavior is not established by the available sources.

title: Signal Graph
text: Signal Graph describes Oliv’s interpretation layer: activity is turned into revenue-relevant context that can be updated as new evidence arrives.

title: Signal Graph · What a signal means
text: A signal can represent an observed risk, qualification detail, stakeholder change, customer need or expansion indication. It is an interpretation grounded in source activity, not an independently guaranteed outcome. The website presents specialized models for revenue questions. This V1 explains the user-facing behavior without treating model counts or accuracy claims as verified benchmarks.

title: Signal Graph · Read the signal with its evidence
text: Identify the question the signal is answering. Check the account or opportunity and the source activity. Distinguish a directly stated fact from an interpretation or recommendation. Check whether newer information changed the signal. Confirm how the signal reaches the relevant agent or workflow.

title: Signal Graph · Illustrative workflow
text: An account conversation indicates that a previously supportive stakeholder has changed roles. The account association gives the signal a business location; the process playbook supplies the escalation rule; an agent can prepare a recommended next step. This example explains the relationship between concepts. It is not a promise that a specific trigger, threshold or escalation is enabled in every workspace.

title: Signal Graph · Rules still requiring confirmation
text: Confidence display, refresh timing, human corrections, conflicting evidence and downstream recalculation need production verification. The documentation should describe those rules once established rather than substituting a generic ‘AI confidence’ explanation. For forecast and health workflows, evaluate the signal against observed outcomes over time. A product example or forecast percentage on a marketing page is not a performance commitment.

title: Process Graph
text: Process Graph supplies company-specific operating context so agents can apply the team’s actual standards rather than generic sales advice.

title: Process Graph · What belongs in the playbook
text: The product presentation includes linked knowledge about the market, personas, prospecting, qualification, sales execution, handoffs, onboarding and customer success. The Oliver document adds ownership, methodology, approvals, territory rules and exceptions. State how the organization currently operates. If a process is aspirational or only proposed, mark that state explicitly. An unapproved process should not silently become the operating rule for customer communications or CRM changes.

title: Process Graph · How process changes are maintained
text: Oliver’s source documentation describes translating leader and RevOps input into structured handbook updates and aligning dependent agents. It also describes proposing learned changes for human sign-off. The exact approval interface, authorized approver, propagation timing, version history and rollback behavior are not established for all deployments. Those are governance requirements to confirm before allowing broad process changes.

title: Process Graph · Illustrative rule
text: A qualification rule can specify what evidence is required before an opportunity advances. An exception can state who may approve advancement when a required stakeholder is unavailable. A useful documentation entry includes the rule, scope, owner, effective date, evidence and exception path. This is a recommended rule format, not a claim that every field is currently configurable in Oliv.

title: Process Graph · Handle conflicting process sources
text: When two documents disagree on authority or a threshold, retain the conflict and ask the accountable owner to resolve it. Recency alone is not a reason to override an approved policy. Use the same approved process vocabulary across agent references, integration mappings and task guides. That prevents a renamed stage or qualification field from receiving several inconsistent explanations.

title: Agent execution and coordination
text: The agent layer combines a defined job, relevant context, available tools and an action boundary. Coordination determines which specialist handles the work.

title: Agent execution and coordination · The parts of an agent workflow
text: Job and instructions Define the intended work and success condition Context Provide the relevant account, opportunity and process knowledge Tools Read or change information through supported connections Trigger or request Start work from a verified event, schedule or user interaction Review boundary Determine what needs human confirmation Run result Show the output, destination and any unresolved issue

title: Agent execution and coordination · Super agents and specialists
text: Olivia is presented as the frontline execution and orchestration agent. Oliver maintains the process and configuration context. Specialist agents focus on particular jobs such as forecast preparation, CRM updates or coaching. The current public pages provide this conceptual distinction. The prototype’s dropdowns and demo run data do not establish production permission enforcement or runtime precedence.

title: Agent execution and coordination · Confirm boundaries per action
text: Separate read-only analysis, draft creation, CRM writes, outbound sending and process configuration. One general ‘autonomous’ label is insufficient to explain those different consequences. For each action, document whose identity is used, who can enable it, whether approval expires, where the request appears, what is logged and how a failed or rejected action is handled. These are acceptance questions until verified.

title: Knowledge and data access
text: An agent’s context can include organization process knowledge, source records and task-specific supporting material. Uploading a file and authorizing a connector are different operations.

title: Knowledge and data access · Types of context
text: Organization playbook Approved operating rules, methodology and exceptions Task-specific knowledge Relevant supporting material for a particular job Connected records Accounts, contacts, opportunities and activity Conversation evidence Recordings, transcripts, email and messages within authorized scope

title: Knowledge and data access · Source and access controls
text: Confirm who may add, replace or remove knowledge, whether access follows the source system, and whether individual or team information can be exposed to other users. The prototype lists import sources and accepted upload formats, but several import actions have no working behavior. A named source is not a confirmed connector; a prototype file-count label is not a commercial storage limit.

title: Knowledge and data access · Lifecycle and updates
text: Document when changed knowledge becomes available to an agent, how obsolete content is replaced, what is retained after removal and whether historical outputs continue to cite the prior version. Treat source provenance as part of the workflow. A current rule and an obsolete document can both be retrievable; the product owner must establish how conflicting or superseded material is handled.

title: Knowledge and data access · Recommended verification
text: Use a controlled document with a distinct fact, update that fact, and check subsequent answers and actions. Remove access and verify that the relevant user and agent cannot continue to retrieve restricted content. Do not claim organization-wide knowledge isolation, automatic deletion from every derived store or a fixed refresh SLA from the current materials.

title: Run history and outputs
text: Run history should help a user explain what an agent attempted, what it produced and what happened next.

title: Run history and outputs · Run concepts
text: Trigger Why work began Input context The record and source information used Attempt A particular execution of the job Output The prepared answer, draft, proposed change or completed action Review state Whether a human decision is required or recorded Destination result What the receiving system accepted or rejected

title: Run history and outputs · What the prototype establishes
text: The extraction records run lists, a details drawer, output presentations and an Agent Feed. Its runs are hand-written examples, predominantly successful, rather than production telemetry. Those examples do not establish complete logging of every action, failure-state coverage, retention, pagination, export or an audit guarantee. A cleared feed row is also not evidence that a run or its source data was deleted.

title: Run history and outputs · Recommended evidence for a support case
text: Agent and workflow name. Time, timezone and initiating event. Account, opportunity or meeting identifier. Observed output and destination. Approval or rejection state if shown. Error text or the point where expected behavior stopped.

title: Run history and outputs · Rules to verify
text: Confirm failed, queued, running, cancelled and retried states; whether retries create new attempts; what the user can correct; and how long history is retained. If native run IDs or logs are unavailable, describe the support process that actually exists. Do not invent a run export API or a retry button.

title: Converse app
text: Converse is the conversation-capture workspace: bring recordings, transcripts and related activity into a searchable source of customer context.

title: Converse app · Capture sources
text: The current app page presents online meetings, phone and in-person capture alongside connected email and messages. Each channel depends on its supported integration and configuration. title: Converse app · Conversation library and context

Searchability and downstream use depend on access to the original recording or transcript. Confirm which users can view, share or export each item and how source permissions are preserved.

title: Converse app · Recording prerequisites

title: Forecast app · Snapshots and change history

They should not be described as one feature. Confirm snapshot frequency, retention and whether corrected source data changes historical views. The prototype includes multiple deal surfaces and does not establish which is the current production grid.

title: Forecast app · Boundaries

text: A supported calendar connection and the relevant meeting. Correct participant and account/opportunity association. Access to prior context and the active qualification framework. A recording or transcript for post-meeting outputs.

title: Prepare and follow up a meeting · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Identify whether this is a first-contact meeting or an active-opportunity discussion. Use Researcher for first-contact background and Meeting Assistant for deal-aware preparation. Send or apply the result using the verified review path and check the destination.

title: Prepare and follow up a meeting · Variations and exceptions

title: Prepare and follow up a meeting · Recommended acceptance checks

Check a first-contact meeting with no opportunity. Change a participant or time and observe refresh behavior. Confirm the approved brief timing and notification channel. Verify that an unsent draft remains distinct from a sent email.

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Before you start

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Workflow sequence
text: This sequence describes the documented handoffs. Verify current production controls before using it as a click-by-click end-user procedure. Open the relevant record and identify the source activity. Review the proposed value and the evidence behind it. Check the field type, destination object and whether newer human edits conflict. Approve, edit or reject through the actual supported review flow. Confirm the final value in the CRM and retain the available change evidence.

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Expected result
text: The intended result is a correctly associated, supported field or record update. A proposed value, a queued write and a CRM-accepted change are different states.

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Variations and exceptions

title: Review and apply CRM updates · Recommended acceptance checks
text: The following checks are proposed validation work, not claims that the product already provides every control mentioned. Test a standard field and a customer-specific mapped field. Reject one proposed change and confirm no write occurs. Compare the acting identity in the CRM with the agreed connector identity. Observe a validation failure and the actual retry/support behavior. Confirm the correction or recovery path for an incorrect update.

title: Run a pipeline review · Before you start

title: Run a pipeline review · Workflow sequence

title: Run a pipeline review · Recommended acceptance checks

Check manager visibility across the intended team only. Confirm the date range and timezone of a summary. Verify the path from a suggested action to an owned next step.

title: Prepare and review a forecast · Before you start

Check a manager adjustment separately from a rep submission. Verify snapshot cadence and whether historical values are preserved. Confirm the criteria for changing automation modes. Measure accuracy against actual outcomes using an agreed definition.

title: Run a coaching cycle · Recommended acceptance checks

Verify who can see the rep’s underlying activity. Correct a scoring error and observe later reporting. Confirm whether the workflow supports the chosen role and motion. Keep illustrative improvement percentages separate from measured results.

text: Different source workflows say ten, twenty or thirty minutes before a meeting. These may describe different products, dates or configurations. The current final rule must be confirmed rather than averaged or selected silently. Post-meeting processing also depends on source availability and completion. ‘After the meeting’ is not enough to establish a service-level commitment.

title: Briefs, reports and cadence · Monthly report versus monthly announcement
text: A monthly coaching report is customer workflow output. A monthly product announcement describes released product changes. A documentation changelog records edits to the documentation. They require separate names, dates and evidence. Use the announcements area for release-note format and the documentation history for V1 changes.

title: API, MCP and developer interfaces
text: The website describes connecting external agent systems through MCP and synchronizing context to other systems. A usable developer reference still requires the actual interface specification.

title: API, MCP and developer interfaces · What the sources establish
text: The public platform presentation describes external access and context synchronization. The prototype contains UI labels such as MCP Servers, but those labels are not an endpoint or tool specification. The historical vault inventory links an Oliv MCP/API guide in ClickUp. That guide could not be retrieved through the available connection during this V1.

title: API, MCP and developer interfaces · Required developer reference
text: Authentication Credential method, scopes, identity and revocation MCP Connection URL, transport, tools, input/output schemas and permissions API Base URL, version, methods, resources and schemas Writes Validation, idempotency, conflict handling and approval boundaries Limits Rate, concurrency, payload and pagination behavior Errors Codes, retry guidance and support correlation Webhooks Events, signing, delivery, ordering and replay if supported SDKs Official packages, compatibility and tested examples if available

title: API, MCP and developer interfaces · No invented endpoint examples
text: This V1 intentionally does not provide runnable API requests, fabricated MCP tool names or webhook payloads. An apparently useful code sample would be misleading without the real contract. Once the guide is accessible, build resource-level reference pages and validate examples against a controlled environment. Add version and deprecation policy separately from marketing copy.

title: Glossary
text: The glossary defines the terms used in this V1. It does not resolve unconfirmed aliases or turn a marketing name into a verified implementation.

title: Glossary · Platform terms
text: Context Capture Bringing supported customer activity into the platform Context Graph Associating activities with relevant accounts, contacts and opportunities Signal Graph Interpreting revenue-relevant questions from source context Process Graph Maintained organization playbook and operating rules Agent A defined job using relevant context and supported actions Super agent The current framing for Olivia and Oliver’s broader coordinating/process jobs App A workspace grouping related revenue tasks Specialist An agent focused on a particular job MCP The external-agent connection interface named in the product presentation; actual contract pending

title: Glossary · Workflow terms
text: Trigger An event, schedule or request that starts work Tool A supported action or source-access capability available to an agent Run An attempt to complete a defined job Draft Prepared content that is not necessarily sent Proposed update A suggested field or record change that is not necessarily written Approval An authorized human decision before a defined action Snapshot A preserved historical view for comparison Submission A forecast entered for a specific cycle Intent The detection brief for Content Curator Library/playlist A destination organizing accessible clips Botless/native recording Recording through the meeting platform under supported setup conditions

title: Glossary · Commercial and review terms
text: Amplify, Converse, Sell and Grow are commercial role groups in the current pricing presentation. Converse also names an app, so the context of the term matters. Documented means the reviewed source describes the behavior. Partial means useful detail exists but important rules remain unresolved. Needs confirmation means the current materials cannot support an operational specification. None of those labels means GA or owner-approved.

title: Glossary · Aliases and former names
text: Keep Deal Assistant, Deal Assist and Meeting Assistant distinct until the product owner confirms which relationships and former names are customer-facing. Likewise, do not merge a prototype forecast-related name into Forecaster based only on similarity. Use the current dedicated page name for navigation and maintain a separate reviewed alias register when the relationship is established.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Troubleshooting begins by separating missing input, incorrect association, incomplete processing, review state and destination failure.

title: Troubleshooting · Recommended diagnostic order
text: Confirm the source activity or record exists and is accessible. Check whether it arrived in Oliv with the correct identity and time. Verify the account, opportunity and participants. Check the relevant agent or workflow state. Determine whether human review is pending. Inspect the destination system and any observed error. Escalate with the minimum useful evidence.

title: Troubleshooting · Support evidence
text: Include the workflow and agent name, time and timezone, relevant record or meeting ID, the expected result, the observed state and any exact error text. Avoid sending unrelated customer content. Do not repeatedly retry a consequential action until you know whether the previous attempt succeeded. The current sources do not establish a universal idempotency or undo mechanism.

title: Meeting capture and brief issues
text: A missing brief and a missing recording can have different causes. Establish the stage that stopped before changing the workflow.

title: Meeting capture and brief issues · Symptoms and checks
text: Meeting not recognized Connected calendar, attendee details, scheduling-tool settings and timezone Visible note taker did not join Organizer, lobby/admission and configured capture route Expected botless capture did not occur Organization native-recording setup and supported platform conditions Recording unavailable Recording permission, completion and access to the artifact Brief missing or late Correct workflow, delivery channel, current schedule and source coverage Wrong opportunity in brief Activity association and multi-deal context Follow-up missing Recording/transcript processing and review state

title: Meeting capture and brief issues · Do not assume one preparation time
text: The available sources describe different preparation windows. Confirm the current product and workspace rule before treating a ten-, twenty- or thirty-minute expectation as a defect. A rescheduled meeting or a changed participant can also affect the input context. The refresh and cutoff rules need production confirmation.

title: Meeting capture and brief issues · Recording controls
text: Use the current recording guide and verified client controls to stop or exclude capture. Older calendar-assistant instructions about Slack availability do not necessarily control the 2026 meeting recorder. If native recording is not enabled, contact the implementation owner for the current platform setup; do not infer a local workaround from a marketing promise.

title: Meeting capture and brief issues · Escalate with
text: Meeting platform, organizer and scheduled time/timezone. Connected calendar and attendee-recognition context. Expected versus observed recording mode. Lobby/admission or permission evidence. Recording or meeting identifier and relevant delivery destination.

title: Integration and sync issues
text: A connected-looking interface does not prove that a particular object or action is authorized and working.

title: Integration and sync issues · Symptoms and checks
text: No source data Account identity, connector authorization and selected scope Some records missing Supported objects, filters, ownership and historical import Wrong account or opportunity Association rules and duplicate or multi-opportunity cases Proposed update not written Approval state, field mapping and writable field type CRM rejected value Provider validation, enumeration, required fields and permissions Notifications missing Destination membership, app permissions and selected channel Old values remain Refresh cadence, conflict policy and source-of-truth rule

title: Integration and sync issues · Recovery boundary
text: Use the connector’s actual reconnect, retry or support path. Reinstalling, widening scopes or recreating records can have broader consequences and should not substitute for finding the failing stage. Confirm whether the receiving system accepted the previous operation before retrying a write or message. The sources do not establish universal duplicate suppression.

title: Integration and sync issues · Escalate with
text: Connector and connected account or tenant. Relevant object and source/destination identifiers. Field or action affected. Observed authorization or validation message. Last known successful sync and the current time/timezone. Whether approval was required and completed.

title: Agent output and execution issues
text: An incorrect answer, an unstarted run and an unperformed action are distinct failures.

title: Agent output and execution issues · Symptoms and checks
text: Output lacks context Source coverage, access and correct account/opportunity Recommendation conflicts with policy Current playbook rule, exception and effective date Configuration appears lost Verified production save/persistence behavior Action did not execute Availability, trigger, permission and approval state Duplicate or unexpected action Concurrent events, retry behavior and ownership No failure details Available run evidence and support correlation path

title: Agent output and execution issues · Prototype evidence is not a production incident
text: The source kit explicitly describes a frontend prototype with nonfunctional actions and local-state settings. Seeing that behavior in its files does not establish the behavior of the live customer product. Use a running environment or a current implementation specification to confirm the issue and the recovery path.

title: Agent output and execution issues · Recommended output review
text: Check the source facts, association, relevant process rule, requested job and destination independently. Correcting a factual input may not correct an ownership or policy error. For consequential output, preserve the proposed result and the observed external-system state. Do not infer that an action happened because a feed row says it did in demonstration data.

title: Agent output and execution issues · Escalate with
text: Agent and initiating request or event. Input record and relevant source evidence. Expected and observed output. Approval or configuration state. Destination result and any error. Whether an earlier attempt may already have succeeded.

title: Announcements and release notes
text: Monthly product announcements should report confirmed product changes with clear availability and action requirements. A documentation draft date is not a product launch date.

title: Announcements and release notes · What a release note needs
text: A stable entry ID and an explicit publication date. The affected product, app, agent or integration. What changed and the customer-visible behavior. GA, beta or rollout conditions and applicable plans. Any action, migration or permission change. A link to the updated current documentation. A responsible owner and verified release evidence.

title: Announcements and release notes · V1 release scope
text: No approved product-release ledger was supplied. This V1 therefore includes a release-note format and a documentation history, without inventing monthly product changes from prototype commits. Current references explain the latest reviewed behavior; announcement archives explain what changed at a known date. Avoid duplicating the entire feature reference in every monthly note.

title: Monthly announcement format
text: This is an editorial template. It is not a record of a released Oliv feature.

title: Monthly announcement format · URL and heading format
text: Use /announcements/YYYY-MM/ for an approved monthly archive and a stable entry anchor such as #crm-manager-reviewed-updates. Give an individual change its own page when the migration or impact needs substantial explanation. Use H2 for a product or change group, H3 for the specific change and H4 for details such as availability, required action or limitations. Explicit IDs should remain stable when the wording of a heading improves. Archive title Month YYYY product updates Entry ID REL-YYYY-MM-001 H3 anchor crm-manager-reviewed-updates Availability Confirmed state, cohort, plan and date Action Required customer step, or explicitly no action Current docs Link to the maintained capability reference

title: Monthly announcement format · Release entry template
text: Change title: state the customer-visible behavior in plain language. What changed: describe the previous and new behavior only when both are verified. Availability: state rollout, plans, prerequisites, regions or restrictions. Action required: give the verified customer step and deadline if one applies. Limitations: state known exceptions or breaking changes. Learn more: link to current setup, reference and troubleshooting pages.

title: Monthly announcement format · Release verification
text: Do not use a source file’s first commit, a marketing-page revision or this V1’s creation date as the product release date. Obtain the release record or the accountable owner’s confirmation. If the exact release date is unknown, keep the entry in the review queue. Do not create an empty dated product archive that suggests a release occurred.

title: Documentation history
text: This history records the documentation artifact and its evidence scope. It does not announce new product capabilities.

title: Documentation history · 16 October 2026 — V1 review draft
text: Created a source-grounded V1 documentation set covering agents, apps, platform concepts, workflows, teams, integrations, administration, reference and troubleshooting. Added stable heading links, search, Markdown downloads and source review. Original source documents and detailed checklist worksheets remain in the private authoring repository.

title: Documentation history · Known review items
text: The first publication review must reconcile current agent availability, naming relationships, permissions and approval enforcement, connector scope, limits, credits, security statements and release dates. Current source conflicts include preparation timing and Engage pricing. No owner approval, production test or product release is implied by the creation of this documentation.

title: V1 review guide
text: This review area is for the documentation team and product owners. It is not an end-user feature catalog or an approved release statement.

title: V1 review guide · Recommended review order
text: Confirm current names and the availability of the agents and apps. Review one end-to-end customer workflow against a running environment. Confirm permissions, approvals and external action identity. Approve connector mappings, limits and commercial terms. Approve security/data-use and release-history statements. Resolve source conflicts and update the relevant page. Choose the approved pages and indexing policy for a public release.

title: V1 review guide · Review deliverables
text: Download the documentation Markdown, page inventory and public source register to review this preview. Return a correction with the page URL, section link, proposed wording and supporting evidence. The live preview is publicly accessible and marked noindex. The full authoring repository, original documents and detailed evidence worksheets remain private.

title: Coverage and checklist review
text: V1 covers the accessible product presentation and documented jobs. It does not claim that every original buyer parameter has been researched and approved.

title: Coverage and checklist review · Source coverage
text: The direct HTTP collection returned 85 successful responses, resolving to 57 distinct page paths: 32 product/navigation pages and 25 listed Help Center articles. Domain aliases and repeated navigation links account for duplicate requests. The eleven original agent documents were retrieved from their shared folder. Relevant Google Docs add use-case and app context. Videos, authenticated production screens, backend code and the ClickUp MCP/API guide were not fully reviewed.

title: Coverage and checklist review · Original checklist baseline
text: The original 555-row checklist and its source evidence are retained in the private documentation repository. This public UI review build omits those worksheet records and the original sixty-question extraction log. All 92 document routes remain available for navigation and content review. A topic appearing in the navigation does not establish product availability or owner approval.

title: Coverage and checklist review · Approval state
text: No claim is marked product-owner approved merely because it has a source. Current feature availability, production permissions, numeric limits and security statements still need accountable confirmation. Review a page by its claims and workflow, not by the number of headings or the presence of a complete template.

title: Source register
text: The register records source type, date and access scope. It does not collapse marketing copy, internal descriptions and production verification into one confidence label.

title: Source register · Source precedence for V1
text: The user designated the latest website navigation and agent pages as the current presentation. Those pages set primary names and framing. Original agent documents add detailed behavior where compatible; older help articles are qualified by their displayed dates. An approved legal or contractual statement is not replaced by newer marketing copy. Conflicts are recorded for the accountable owner rather than resolved through recency alone.

title: Source register · Retrieved sources
text: This hosted register contains the 57 public product and Help Center sources. Private document identifiers, Drive links and source metadata are excluded. A retrieval date records when a source was checked; it is not a product release or owner-approval date.

title: Source register · Limitations
text: Public citations are shown where available. Additional source materials and detailed evidence remain in the private authoring repository. This preview publishes authored documentation, not raw source documents or a mirror of the research collection.

title: Open questions and claim conflicts
text: The original kit raised sixty open questions. This V1 adds a smaller, prioritized publication queue that consolidates the most consequential unresolved claims.

title: Open questions and claim conflicts · Publication review queue
Open questions and claim conflicts · How to return an answer
text: Include the question ID, affected page and section, approved wording, evidence or demonstration, accountable reviewer and effective date. If the answer is rollout-specific, identify the eligible workspaces, plans and conditions. An answer saying only ‘yes’ is insufficient when the question concerns scope, permissions, costs or lifecycle. Record the exception path and actual user-visible behavior.

title: Open questions and claim conflicts · Original question log
text: The original sixty-question extraction log is retained in the private repository. The concise publication-review queue above identifies the product facts that need confirmation. Close a question only when its specific behavior and applicable scope have been verified.

title: Legacy help and naming migration
text: The Help Center mixes calendar-assistant material from 2018–2020 with later revenue-workflow articles and a May 2026 recording guide.

title: Legacy help and naming migration · Recommended disposition
text: Calendar-driven Slack status/DND Confirm legacy product scope; keep outside current revenue agent instructions Older Outlook add-in guidance Verify current clients, tenant policy and installation procedure 2024 integration and meeting guides Update setup routes, scopes, capture modes and timings 2026 recording modes Preserve conditional behavior; verify current platform-specific setup Prototype agent names Resolve aliases and rollout before merging Draft app landing copy Use for intent and concepts; validate actions and commercial claims

title: Legacy help and naming migration · URLs and redirects
text: Do not delete or redirect a legacy help URL simply because it is old. First determine whether customers still use that product and whether the replacement covers the same task. When a replacement is approved, preserve the task intent, add an explicit migration note and plan the redirect or archive status. Fragment identifiers also need consideration when headings are renamed.

title: Legacy help and naming migration · Specific conflicts
text: Meeting-prep timing differs across older help flows and September agent documents. The current Engage page and pricing page also disagree on the starting/add-on presentation. The older Outlook calendar workaround and the broad certification lists in derived documents require responsible-owner review before reuse.

title: Documentation contract and publishing
text: The documentation is authored for clear user tasks and source accountability. Machine-readable delivery should reflect the same approved content that a person reads.

title: Documentation contract and publishing · URLs and section IDs
text: Use lowercase, hyphenated path segments and one canonical route per distinct task or reference. Keep route depth shallow; this V1 has no route deeper than three path segments. Every H2, H3 and H4 has an explicit stable ID and a copyable section link. The URL path locates the document; the fragment locates its section. Changing a heading’s wording should not change its ID.

title: Documentation contract and publishing · Heading hierarchy
text: Use one H1 for the page title, H2 for major sections, H3 for subordinate topics and H4 only for a meaningful detail.

title: Documentation contract and publishing · Fragment behavior
text: Use ordinary fragment links such as /agents/crm-manager/#actions-and-review. The fragment is resolved in the browser and is not a separate server resource or sitemap URL.

title: Documentation contract and publishing · Content model
text: The canonical source is lib/content.json. Each page has a URL, title, description, summary, sections, sources, evidence status and availability note. Sections carry stable IDs and can contain prose, steps, lists, tables and subordinate sections. Markdown and downloads are generated review exports. Editing an export alone does not update the site. Page and section IDs should remain stable when a source changes.

title: Documentation contract and publishing · Readable delivery
text: The static build includes the full authored content in HTML without requiring client-side rendering. Navigation, breadcrumbs, section links and related references are ordinary links. Search adds convenience without being the only way to discover a page. The build generates Markdown downloads, a route/metadata inventory, a sitemap and optional llms.txt and llms-full.txt aids. Those aids do not guarantee crawling, understanding or citation by an AI system.

title: Documentation contract and publishing · Review and production indexing
text: This live preview is public and marked noindex. The full authoring repository and original evidence worksheets remain private. Robots directives do not provide access control. Before an official product documentation launch, approve the claims, choose the production origin, confirm the access policy and regenerate indexing files.

title: Documentation contract and publishing · Operational controls for a future public site
text: Use normal caching, conditional requests, observability and measured rate limits. Keep the main documentation readable without a challenge on every request; escalate controls based on observed abuse. Do not hide different factual content from humans and bots, generate thin keyword variants, or publish unverified capabilities to influence AI answers. Content accuracy and access policy take priority over crawler volume.

title: Documentation contract and publishing · Maintenance
text: Assign owners for product behavior, integration contracts, commercial terms and security claims. Re-review pages when those underlying facts change. Use the documentation history for editorial changes and the announcement archive for verified product releases. A publication check should validate claims, links, anchors, metadata, generated exports, mobile navigation and search. Technical correctness does not substitute for product-owner approval.
